description: Compare solid 3cos(2x+4) and dashed cos(2x+4) with common zeros and extrema abscissas, retaining the vertical crest guide and horizontal amplitude-3 guide. Modern window endpoints are not domain restrictions.

authoritativeText.text:
2) 考虑数平面到自身的映射：
$(x,y)\longrightarrow(x,ky)\qquad(k>0)$。
当 $k<1$ 时，称为向 $Ox$ 轴以 $1:k$ 的比例压缩；

当 $k>1$ 时，称为向 $Ox$ 轴以 $1:k$ 的比例伸长。
本课把“压缩”和“伸长”统称为“压缩”，在两种情形下都采用这一说法。
由函数 $f$ 的图象经过上述映射，可以得到下列函数的图象：
$g(x)=kf(x)$。

事实上，方程 $y=f(x)$ 和 $ky=g(x)$ 同解。
第一个方程表示点 $(x,y)$ 在函数 $f$ 的图象上，第二个方程表示对应点 $(x,ky)$ 在函数 $g$ 的图象上。

3) 数平面到自身的映射
$(x,y)\longrightarrow(kx,y)$
称为向 $Oy$ 轴以 $1:k$ 的比例压缩，其中 $k>0$。

由函数 $f$ 的图象经过这一映射，可以得到下列函数的图象：
$g(x)=f\left(\frac{x}{k}\right)$。

事实上，$g(kx)=f\left(\frac{kx}{k}\right)=f(x)$，因此方程 $y=f(x)$ 和 $y=g(kx)$ 同解。
第一个方程表示点 $(x,y)$ 在函数 $f$ 的图象上，第二个方程表示对应点 $(kx,y)$ 在函数 $g$ 的图象上。

4) 下面说明如何由余弦函数的图象得到下列函数的图象：
$y=A\cos(\omega x+\varphi),\ A>0,\ \omega>0\qquad(1)$。
$\blacktriangleright$ 按照前面的第三条图象变换规则，将 $y=\cos x$ 的图象向 $Oy$ 轴以 $1:\frac{1}{\omega}$ 的比例压缩，就得到函数 $\cos\omega x$ 的图象。
将所得图象向右（当 $\varphi<0$ 时）或向左（当 $\varphi>0$ 时）平移 $\frac{|\varphi|}{\omega}$ 的距离，就得到函数 $\cos(\omega x+\varphi)$ 的图象。

最后，按照第二条规则，将所得图象向 $Ox$ 轴以 $k=\frac{1}{A}$ 的比例压缩，就得到函数(1)的图象。
$\blacktriangleleft$
这里的比例不能直接作为前面点映射中的坐标倍率使用。

下文的变换汇总列出了实际的缩放比例。

函数(1)的图象可以由余弦函数的图象依次通过下列变换得到：
1) 向 $Oy$ 轴以 $1:\frac{1}{\omega}$ 的比例压缩；
2) 平移 $\vec r\left(-\frac{\varphi}{\omega},0\right)$；

3) 向 $Ox$ 轴以 $1:A$ 的比例压缩。

例3 函数 $y=3\cos(2x+4)$ 的图象可以由余弦函数的图象依次通过下列变换得到：
1) 向 $Oy$ 轴以 $1:\frac{1}{2}$ 的比例压缩（图18）；
2) 平移 $\vec r(-2,0)$（图19）；

3) 向 $Ox$ 轴以 $1:3$ 的比例压缩（图20）。

inventory.description: One Cartesian frame with right/up arrowheads, x/y labels and an oval origin glyph below/left of the crossing. No grid. Quantitative provenance: Cartesian origin from the edition; original glyph codepoint remains UNKNOWN. Exact finite display cuts and original O/0 glyph remain UNKNOWN; modern O are declared editorial naming additions. Curve coordinates are calculated from approved edition functions, not measured from pixels.

Solid large-amplitude curve labelled y=3cos(2x+4). Four positive crests and four negative troughs, with near-axis upward-going cuts on both ends. At origin it is negative and rising. Quantitative provenance: Example3 supplies vertical factor 3 after the translation. All analytical coordinates are text-derived; cuts are not assigned domain endpoints. Exact finite display cuts and original O/0 glyph remain UNKNOWN; modern O are declared editorial naming additions. Curve coordinates are calculated from approved edition functions, not measured from pixels.

Dashed smaller-amplitude curve, same phase and same zero crossings as the solid curve. Four positive crests and four negative troughs; its troughs/crests align vertically with the corresponding solid extrema. Both near-axis outer branches rise. Short crossing-adjacent strokes are not reliably separate numerical labels. Quantitative provenance: Reference is y=cos(2x+4) by the preceding step, not a different phase or baseline cosine. Exact finite display cuts and original O/0 glyph remain UNKNOWN; modern O are declared editorial naming additions. Curve coordinates are calculated from approved edition functions, not measured from pixels.

A dashed vertical guide at the second crest from the left connects the horizontal axis, the dashed crest and the solid crest. No readable x value is printed there. A dashed horizontal guide at the top-amplitude level extends from near the y-axis toward the next solid crest to its right. The y value 3 is printed just left of that level. Quantitative provenance: 3 is source-readable and edition-stated. The vertical guide's x=-2 and its crest heights 1/3 follow from the edition and the identified crest, not a recovered source x label. The right crest's exact abscissa is likewise text-derived. Exact finite display cuts and original O/0 glyph remain UNKNOWN; modern O are declared editorial naming additions. Curve coordinates are calculated from approved edition functions, not measured from pixels.
